source: First 25 canonical legacy identities in data/v2-audit/current-question-audit.json order.

current.prompt: I consider how change might affect relationships before moving forward.

proposed.prompt: When change could improve the situation but disrupt important relationships, I prefer to protect continuity with people before accelerating it.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether preserving relationships and continuity naturally outweighs faster change.

questions.why: The Yellow motive is valuable, but the current wording rewards generic consideration without making the competing priority visible.

current.prompt: I’m comfortable being the one who takes the heat if a decision doesn’t work out.

proposed.prompt: After I own a mistake, my attention moves quickly to the decision that will get things back on track.

replacement.prompt: After I own a mistake, my attention moves quickly to the decision that will get things back on track.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: restoring progress vs. remaining with the failure
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether attention moves naturally from owning a mistake to restoring progress.

questions.why: Taking the heat can measure courage or duty; the approved candidate exposes the Red recovery motive directly.

current.prompt: It is important to me that social settings always ensure everyone feels included and comfortable.

proposed.prompt: When a workable group decision is ready, I’m more comfortable delaying it to hear from the people most affected than moving ahead and gathering their feedback afterward.

replacement.prompt: When a workable group decision is ready, I’m more comfortable delaying it to hear from the people most affected than moving ahead and gathering their feedback afterward.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether affected people having a voice naturally outweighs immediate group closure.

questions.why: The current absolute wording makes inclusion an obvious virtue; the candidate presents two defensible priorities.

current.prompt: When a decision needs to be made, I usually…

options.wording: decide fast and move
talk it out and go with what feels exciting
look for the option that’s fairest for everyone
ask questions until it’s clear

proposed.prompt: A group has several good ideas but cannot settle on one direction. What contribution comes most naturally to you?

options.label: Narrow the choices and recommend the direction most likely to deliver
Explore whether the strongest ideas can create a more exciting possibility
Look for the direction the group can support and sustain together
Define criteria and compare how well each idea meets them

replacement.prompt: A group has several good ideas but cannot settle on one direction. What contribution comes most naturally to you?

options.wording: Narrow the choices and recommend the direction most likely to deliver
Explore whether the strongest ideas can create a more exciting possibility
Look for the direction the group can support and sustain together
Define criteria and compare how well each idea meets them

option_to_color.wording: Narrow the choices and recommend the direction most likely to deliver
Explore whether the strongest ideas can create a more exciting possibility
Look for the direction the group can support and sustain together
Define criteria and compare how well each idea meets them

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: delivery vs. possibility vs. shared support vs. criteria
measurement.what_it_measures: Which motivation a person contributes when several workable directions compete.

questions.why: The legacy Yellow option sounds morally superior and the Blue option is compound; the candidate balances four useful decision contributions.

current.prompt: If someone is upset with me, I tend to…

options.wording: address it directly and quickly
try to lighten it up and reset the vibe
listen and apologize if needed
ask for specifics and clarify what happened

proposed.prompt: Someone tells you they are upset about something you did. What do you most naturally want to establish first?

options.label: The clearest path to resolving the issue
A more open tone where new understanding can emerge
What affected the relationship and would restore trust
The specific facts and where our interpretations differ

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: resolution vs. openness vs. trust repair vs. factual clarity
measurement.what_it_measures: What a person seeks first when repairing an interpersonal disagreement.

questions.why: The current apology option is uniquely virtuous and the Blue option can sound avoidant; the revision makes each first priority useful.

current.prompt: I feel uneasy benefiting if it means someone else is treated unfairly.

measurement.what_it_measures: Discomfort with benefiting from unfair treatment.

questions.why: Agreement primarily endorses fairness as a universal virtue rather than a distinct Yellow relational preference.

current.prompt: I prefer steady, predictable income over high-risk opportunities.

proposed.prompt: When two options are similarly worthwhile, I prefer the one with more predictable consequences to the one with more upside and uncertainty.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether predictable consequences naturally outweigh uncertain upside.

questions.why: The construct fits Green, but income and financial circumstances confound the current version.

current.prompt: I’m careful not to rush change if people around me aren’t ready.

proposed.prompt: When a change could improve the situation quickly but disrupt people’s existing commitments, I tend to favor a slower transition.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: commitment continuity vs. speed of improvement
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether protecting commitments naturally outweighs faster change.

questions.why: The current wording sounds like universally responsible change management; the revision exposes the priority and cost.

current.prompt: My ideal workday feels like…

options.wording: progress and measurable wins
variety, people, and momentum
steady teamwork and support
structure, clarity, and focus time

proposed.prompt: My ideal workday feels like…

options.label: progress and measurable wins
variety, people, and momentum
steady teamwork and support
structure, clarity, and focus time

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: wins vs. variety vs. support vs. structure
measurement.what_it_measures: Which kind of workday environment feels naturally rewarding.

questions.why: All four options are attractive and expose recognizable work-environment preferences without a correct answer.

current.prompt: I enjoy social events more when I know what to expect ahead of time.

proposed.prompt: I enjoy a social event more when I know the setting and plan beforehand than when the evening is left open.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether predictability enhances social enjoyment more than an open-ended experience.

questions.why: The revision makes the comparison explicit and reduces the risk of measuring social anxiety alone.

current.prompt: I get restless if I’m stuck at home too long without something fun planned.

proposed.prompt: An afternoon unexpectedly becomes free with no obligations. What are you most naturally drawn to do?

options.label: Use the time to make visible progress on something I want to accomplish
Choose something spontaneous, social, or new that feels energizing
Spend the time in a comfortable way with someone I care about
Dive into something I have wanted time to understand properly

replacement.prompt: An afternoon unexpectedly becomes free with no obligations. What are you most naturally drawn to do?

options.wording: Use the time to make visible progress on something I want to accomplish
Choose something spontaneous, social, or new that feels energizing

Dive into something I have wanted time to understand properly

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: progress vs. novelty vs. closeness vs. understanding
measurement.what_it_measures: What naturally attracts someone when free time has no obligations.

questions.why: The legacy statement conflates confinement, boredom, fun, and planning; the candidate offers a balanced ordinary-life choice.

current.prompt: When plans change suddenly, I…

options.wording: adapt fast and push forward
roll with it if it’s interesting
worry about how it impacts people
want time to re-check the details

proposed.prompt: A plan you were counting on changes with little warning. What matters most in your first response?

options.label: Finding the best available direction so progress does not stall
Seeing what new possibilities the change opens up
Protecting the people and commitments affected by the change
Rebuilding enough clarity to understand what happens next

replacement.prompt: A plan you were counting on changes with little warning. What matters most in your first response?

options.wording: Finding the best available direction so progress does not stall
Seeing what new possibilities the change opens up

Rebuilding enough clarity to understand what happens next

option_to_color.wording: Finding the best available direction so progress does not stall
Seeing what new possibilities the change opens up

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: progress vs. possibility vs. commitments vs. clarity
measurement.what_it_measures: Which established motivation receives attention first when a relied-upon plan changes.

questions.why: The candidate replaces worry and generic adaptability with four explicit, equally reasonable motivations.

current.prompt: I’m more confident moving forward when there’s a clear plan instead of improvising.

proposed.prompt: I’m more confident moving forward when there’s a clear plan instead of improvising.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether a clear plan creates more confidence than improvisation.

questions.why: The wording is concise, non-virtuous, and directly measures an established Green preference.

current.prompt: Your natural reaction to conflict is:

options.wording: Confront it
Diffuse it
Avoid it
Analyze it

proposed.prompt: You and a sibling remember an important family event differently, but no practical decision depends on agreeing. What would you most naturally want from the conversation?

options.label: A clear conclusion about the main point so the disagreement can close
A lively exchange that leaves room for both versions of the story
Understanding how each version connects to what matters to each of us
Clarity about what can be verified and what genuinely remains uncertain

replacement.prompt: You and a sibling remember an important family event differently, but no practical decision depends on agreeing. What would you most naturally want from the conversation?

options.wording: A clear conclusion about the main point so the disagreement can close
A lively exchange that leaves room for both versions of the story
Understanding how each version connects to what matters to each of us
Clarity about what can be verified and what genuinely remains uncertain

option_to_color.wording: A clear conclusion about the main point so the disagreement can close
A lively exchange that leaves room for both versions of the story
Understanding how each version connects to what matters to each of us

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: closure vs. expressive exchange vs. mutual meaning vs. verifiable clarity
measurement.what_it_measures: What resolution a person naturally wants when disagreement does not require action.

questions.why: The legacy mapping incorrectly makes avoidance Blue and reduces Yellow to diffusion; the candidate offers four grounded conflict preferences.

current.prompt: I’m comfortable being the one who takes the heat if a decision doesn’t work out.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: personal accountability vs. avoidance of blame
measurement.what_it_measures: Comfort accepting consequences for a failed decision.

questions.why: It is an exact duplicate of another legacy item and the shared wording measures courage/duty more than Red motivation.

current.prompt: Too much structure makes me feel boxed in or restless.

proposed.prompt: Too much structure makes me feel boxed in or restless.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether heavy structure naturally feels constraining.

questions.why: The item captures a clear Blue/Green preference tension without making either side more competent or mature.

current.prompt: I enjoy bringing people together and helping everyone feel connected.

proposed.prompt: I feel more settled deepening a dependable relationship than widening my circle with new connections.

replacement.prompt: I feel more settled deepening a dependable relationship than widening my circle with new connections.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether dependable relational depth feels more settling than expanding one's social circle.

questions.why: The legacy statement rewards inclusive sociability and can attract Blue; the candidate isolates Yellow depth against a valid Blue preference.

current.prompt: I get uncomfortable when things feel disorganized or unclear.

proposed.prompt: When a workable plan is still loosely defined, I prefer to add structure before proceeding rather than organize it as I go.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether adding structure before action feels more natural than organizing during action.

questions.why: The current discomfort wording is vague and virtue-adjacent; the revision presents two workable styles.

current.prompt: I care a lot about being fair, even when it’s uncomfortable.

measurement.what_it_measures: Willingness to uphold fairness despite discomfort.

questions.why: Agreement mainly claims moral courage and fairness, both universal virtues rather than diagnostic Yellow motivation.

current.prompt: I enjoy measuring progress through income, rank, or performance.

proposed.prompt: I feel most motivated when progress can be measured against a clear target or standard.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: measurable achievement vs. less externally visible progress
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether visible progress against a standard naturally strengthens motivation.

questions.why: The Red construct is established, but income and rank unnecessarily narrow it toward status and occupation.

current.prompt: I’m more productive when I enjoy the process, not just the outcome.

measurement.what_it_measures: Belief that enjoying a process improves productivity.

questions.why: The statement is broadly true across colors and measures a productivity belief rather than Blue personality preference.

current.prompt: I like having systems in place so I don’t have to guess what to do next.

proposed.prompt: I would rather use a repeatable process that gives consistent results than improvise a different approach each time.

replacement.prompt: I would rather use a repeatable process that gives consistent results than improvise a different approach each time.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether consistent repeatability feels preferable to improvising each time.

questions.why: The candidate states a balanced process preference; the legacy wording frames systems as relief from not knowing what to do.

current.prompt: I’m selective about social events and don’t feel the need to attend everything.

measurement.what_it_measures: Preference to attend fewer social events.

questions.why: Introversion or social selectivity alone is explicitly non-diagnostic and does not establish a Green evidence/structure motive.

current.prompt: I don’t mind a little chaos if it leads to progress.

proposed.prompt: When progress is strong, I can tolerate a loosely organized process rather than stop to impose more structure.

measurement.what_it_measures: Whether preserving momentum naturally outweighs tightening process structure.

questions.why: The current 'chaos' wording can attract Blue spontaneity; the revision anchors tolerance to the Red outcome motive.
